reason: The 44 statements come from fern floras (Flora Malesiana series II, PhytoKeys ferns). There the rhizome scales are flat outgrowths of the epidermis (paleae), not leaves. The rhizome is a shoot axis, and PO lists 'scale' as a synonym of trichome, so shoot axis trichome is right. This matches the accepted rule for 'stem scale' (R2828). Angiosperm scale leaves on a rhizome have their own PO class, rhizome scale leaf (PO_0025278). The angiosperm wording 'scale leaves' does not match this key. Older curation files put the fern rhizome scales under PO_0025278 and should be fixed.
Plural of the accepted 'stem scale' rule (R2828) and the same reading as R2829. In ferns these are epidermal scales on the stem or rhizome, which is a shoot axis trichome in PO terms.

Same reading as the accepted rules 'perianth part', 'perianth parts' and 'perianth segment(s)' mapped to tepal (R2259-R2262). Where calyx and corolla are distinct, the floras name them sepals and petals, and those words win. Bristle-like members go to perianth bristle (FLOPO_0986044).

The earlier review read the 27 statements as the middle lobe of a three-lobed orchid labellum. A limit by part name cannot separate the corolla lip of Lamiaceae from the labellum. Lamiaceae floras usually write 'lower lip' or 'middle lobe of lower lip', which do not match this key. 'Middle' cannot be expressed yet, so the position is dropped, as for the other lobe rules.
Same phrase in a different word order as R2841, with the same reading and the same caveat about the corolla lip.

Phyllary maps to involucral bract by the accepted rule C250. Dropping a position word the ontology cannot express is the accepted practice: 'outer tunic' maps to tunic (R2431), and lip midlobe likewise. The inner bract is still an involucral bract, so the statement stays true for that part. Differences between inner and outer bracts are a matter for the contradiction checks.
Plural of R2845, same reading.

Corona lobe is defined as one of the divisions of a floral corona. The thread-like filaments of a Passiflora corona are such divisions. This matches the accepted rules 'corona filament(s)' and 'filament of corona' (R2642-R2644) and 'corona scale' (R2622). The first check read corona lobe too narrowly, as only the asclepiad or daffodil type.
Plural of R2847. It matches the accepted 'corona filaments' rule (R2643).

An ochreola is the sheath of fused bracts around a flower cluster or pedicel in Polygonaceae. FLOPO's ochrea class is defined as fused stipules around the stem node, so it does not fit. PO defines inflorescence bract as a bract borne on the inflorescence axis, which fits. This also brings the rule in line with R2872 ('ochreole' maps to PO_0009054).
Plural of ochreola. Same reason as R2853, and in line with R2872.
Spelling variant of ochreola. Same reason as R2853.
Plural of the ocreola spelling. Same reason as R2853.

PO lists 'knee root' as a synonym of pneumatophore, so the target is right for the knees of Taxodium and mangroves. But 'knee' alone is also a bent node (grasses, bamboo, geniculate parts). Taxon names cannot be used as a limit, so the rule is limited to root context.
Plural of R2860, with the same ambiguity and the same limit.

PO defines flower bract as a bract that subtends the perianth of a flower. The staminate flowers of Carex, Cyperaceae and catkins have no perianth or a reduced one. A scale on the spike or catkin axis below a flower or cymule fits PO's inflorescence bract ('borne on the inflorescence axis below any branch or flower'). The male state belongs to the flower, not the scale.
Plural of R2867. Same reason.

The statements describe a woody, truncate or toothed cup that persists and widens under the fruit, as in Lauraceae. That cup carries the tepals and stamens on its rim, which is PO's hypanthium, and PO lists 'floral cup' as its synonym. A cup of fused tepals alone would be perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010), as the rule's note already says. I kept it on the earlier review's reading of the statements. I did not check other families.
Leaf lamina epidermis is right for the faces of a leaf. But 'faces' alone also means the faces of a petal, seed, valve, glume or fruit. The rule is limited to leaf context.

The French 'loge pollinique' already has its own rules (R2881, R2882). The English key 'pollen chamber' is a pollen sac only in anthers. In gymnosperm ovules it is a cavity in the nucellus. The limit to anther and stamen parts keeps the translated Myristicaceae statements and blocks the ovule sense.

'Floret tube' means the corolla tube of an Asteraceae floret, and PO already lists 'Asteraceae floret' as a synonym of flower. Grass florets have no tube, so the phrase does not occur for grasses. A limit by part name would add nothing, since the key already contains 'floret'.
Plural of R2891, same reading.
'Falls' are the outer tepals only in Iris and its relatives. 'Fall' is otherwise a verb or means leaf fall, so the rule is limited to flower and perianth context.

Separate glands on top of an inferior ovary are not always parts of a disc. This follows the precedent of 'interstaminal gland' (R2339), which was mapped to the general gland class because disc gland was too specific.

The woolly, spine-bearing areola of cacti is PO's areole bud. In leaf venation, an areole is the small area between veins (leaf lamina areole, PO_0025392). The rule is limited to stem, tubercle and spine context.
Same as R2911. Areoles in venation must go to PO_0025392.

In Pottiaceae and similar mosses the peristome is the exostome alone. Its teeth are split into filiform divisions, often called filaments ('32 filaments'), and these are the peristome teeth. The endostome has segments and cilia, not filaments, so the first check's objection does not apply.

A sedge spikelet scale sits on the spikelet axis below a flower that has no perianth or only bristles. So PO's flower bract (a bract below the perianth) does not fit, but inflorescence bract does. This target also covers grass glumes, so no limit is needed. Note that PO glume sits under inflorescence bract.
French form of 'spikelet scale'. Same reason as R2915.

In French floras 'nucule' means the nutlet of a fruit that splits into one-seeded parts (Boraginaceae, Lamiaceae, Verbenaceae), and these are PO mericarps. The Chara sense (oogonium) does not occur in these vascular plant floras. A limit by taxon cannot be written as part names.
